gate_scope_statement.frozen: before the first execution run (module docstring is the source)

gates.gate1_final_touch: terminal control frame: >=1 fingertip pad per hand with pad-to-face distance <= 1.163697e-04 m and touch point z in [0.732, 0.77] m. NOT measured: force closure, lift, posture similarity to the video.
gates.gate2_contact: >=1 control frame per hand with a hand-vs-box-end-face contact. NOT: table contact, pad count, duration.
gates.gate3_approach_clean: zero hand-vs-support contact over the WHOLE clip (any support contact is reported, approach or not). NOT: hand-vs-box contact.
gates.gate4_joint_limits: commands inside ctrlrange INTERSECT jnt range; realised finger qpos inside jnt range; servo winding gates re-derived per side on this run's histories (position, hinge rate, slide rate). Any 1-8 mrad command-boundary transient is explained ONLY from this run's own torque balance; the smoke-5 explanation is not reused.
gates.gate5_palm_deviation: P1 palm deviation: constrained-solve palm/fingertip world deviation AND physics execution deviation, each against the cap. NOT: fingertip tracking vs the video.

honesty_clauses: bridged/held HaMeR frames are listed per side; gates are measured on executed sim contact state, so no bridged frame can fabricate a touch
if a hand's terminal segment had no real detections this report would say blocked; the detection table below is the evidence that it does not

terminal_target_provenance.rule: TARGET vs TRAJECTORY, recorded separately: the terminal touch state is ANCHORED to the v3 gate3 seed (a physics-verified pose: registration anchor + terminal alignment both aim at it), so the acceptance criteria are decided by that seed, NOT by HaMeR. The HaMeR streams shape the trajectory only; their occlusion-phase accuracy (left conf 0.52-0.68 on the grasp window, smoke 6's documented P1 limitation) therefore degrades trajectory fidelity without touching the terminal criterion.

table_clearance_clamp.strategy: explicit z lower-bound clamp: raise the base-z command by the per-frame deficit so the lowest hand collision geom clears the table by >= 30 mm; disclosed substitute for the unusable MANO depth axis

terminal_target_provenance.gate3_seed_file: runs/w6/gate3_qpos.json @ commit cc16641 (round-3: 2 pads per hand in the end-face rectangle mid-band; Main-verified micro-metre)
terminal_target_provenance.gate3_seed_note: the scene test rewrites this file atomically on each run; the seed is anchored by reading the qpos array at runtime and by the cc16641 blob in the report provenance

source.bridge_frame_disclosure: per-side bridged/held frames are listed in per_side.*.bridged_video_frames and held_from_first_detection_video_frames (Main-approved policy: interior gaps <= 3 frames bridged, leading gap holds the first detection; every bridged frame is listed)
source.executed_window_rationale: the box-centre y-curve of the HaMeR detections rises from f17 (lift onset) and the clip ends f34-39 with the hands OPEN beside the box (released). The contracted W6b trajectory is 'approach + pad touch terminal state', so the executed window ends at grasp completion; lift/hold/lower/release is W6c scope. Frozen from source data before any physics run.

smoothing.why: HaMeR frames are independent per-frame estimates (uncorrelated jitter); 3 frames = 1.00 s at 3 fps averages that out while staying at least 2x shorter than the task's own timescales (approach ~12 frames, lift ~7 frames). The constrained solve's signed rate band is the second, command-side low-pass.

wrist_lateral_motion.scale_check: MANO dy over the approach = 3.7 cm matches the pixel-level box-centre curve (dy ~3.4 cm), so the image-plane metric scale transfers 1:1; the depth axis does not (4.8-6.3 m absolute) and is excluded

thumb_axis_check.rule: reflection about the registered base-frame plane perpendicular to the measured thumb axis (M = I - 2 n n^T): preserves the grasp direction and the finger axis, flips only the thumb

mirror_convention_selection.rule: the reflection whose dry base solve is feasible (no hand-geom box penetration, palm plate clearance) with more grasp tips and the smaller closest gap; chosen BEFORE any physics execution, both records kept. Mirrors act on the REGISTERED cloud (post grasp_registration), in the URDF base frame.

right.metric_check: geomDistance reproduces the contact distance exactly where a contact exists (this run: left -21.6913 mm vs contact -21.6913 mm)
right.note: gate3's stored gap is its own deepest recorded touch geom, not necessarily the pad this metric finds first; the calibration proves the METRIC (geomDistance == contact dist), not equality with gate3's bookkeeping

left.metric_check: geomDistance reproduces the contact distance exactly where a contact exists (this run: left -21.9920 mm vs contact -21.9920 mm)
left.note: gate3's stored gap is its own deepest recorded touch geom, not necessarily the pad this metric finds first; the calibration proves the METRIC (geomDistance == contact dist), not equality with gate3's bookkeeping

registration.derivation: R_reg = R_scene_grasp @ R_human_grasp^-1; human side = chordal L2 mean of MANO global_orient over the grasp window; scene side = palm world orientation at the gate-3 pose with the object free joint restored to (0,0,0.74). Per-frame rotation dynamics preserved.

search.objective: minimise the closest fingertip-to-box gap over the whole clip, subject to zero hand-geom interpenetration of the box at every frame. The box is not moved; only the hand's base is solved.
search.grasp_axis: x (the box's 120 mm span, frozen in the MJCF)
search.feasibility: no hand geom may interpenetrate the box, and the palm collision plate must stay a full fingertip-pad radius off it, at every frame

anchor.grasp_tips_note: at the closest-approach frame 2 of 4 fingertips are within 15 mm of the box

constrained_solve.method: temporally coupled solve: alternating projection onto {actuator ctrlrange INTERSECT joint range} and onto the signed velocity band, with a damped Gauss-Newton step between them on the hand world-pose objective (palm frame origin + all four fingertips) using MuJoCo's analytic body Jacobians. No per-frame independent IK.
constrained_solve.objective: sum_t ||hand_world(x_t) - hand_world(x_retargeted)||^2 over the palm frame origin and the four fingertips

hand_world_pose_deviation.definition: how far the constrained solve moved the hand in the world away from the pose the retargeted clip asked for, split into the palm frame (the hand's base pose) and the worst fingertip

fingertips.definition: worst of the four fingertips' ||solved - retargeted|| world positions, per frame

constraints.slide_move_cap_note: per-frame wrist-slide movement from the retargeted command is bounded by cap/sqrt(3) per axis, so the palm frame's world position cannot leave a ball of that radius; the palm frame origin is hand_root + slides exactly

constrained_solve.box_intersection_note: the box is the actuator ctrlrange INTERSECT the joint range; the retargeter commands several finger joints outside both

right.unreachable_note: a DoF counted here holds a tracking error above the tolerance at the first commanded pose, which on this scene is sustained box contact: a finger in contact holds a contact-deflection error rather than the commanded value, and a wrist slide on the list means the commanded descent itself is outside the floating wrist's reachable set -- no approach path reaches it. The ramp caps the *command* rate; it cannot make an unreachable pose reachable. On this run every wrist DoF delivered the commanded pose; the shortfall is on the finger joints only.
right.wrist_reachable_note: per-DoF reachability, dual-hand scene: on the superseded single-hand scene the finding was the opposite -- the palm rested on the box top and the commanded wrist descent was unreachable outright. Kept as a recorded finding so the change of scene is visible rather than silent.

rate_caps.source: free-space step/ramp measurement of this model's own servos (hinges 1.5 rad/s, wrist_y 0.2 m/s), tightened per axis to the servo's own derived winding allowance where the W6a re-scale put that below the measurement (x/z: 45 N / 280 = 0.1607 m/s); recorded in rerun_evidence.velocity_gate.floating_wrist_servo_ceiling

servo_winding_rate.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per wrist hinge: (1) realised rate <= |forcerange|/dof_damping, (2) at most 3 consecutive control intervals above that same cap, (3) every interval in which the servo outran the command-side trackable rate 1.5 rad/s has its excess over the commanded rate explained as this DoF's own wind-up release (release_j(t) = sqrt(kp_j * windup_j(t)^2 / (dof_M0_j + armature_j)), windup_j(t) = ctrl_j(t) - qpos_j(t)) with the actuator off its force limit. kv = 0 does not weaken the bound: dof_damping = 1.2 is what makes a finite bound exist at all. The bound is tight -- the free-space step asymptote of this servo plateaus at 4.90-4.97 rad/s (both directions, both step signs), within 2% of it; with dof_damping forced to 0 the plateau disappears entirely.

dv <= a_max * tau_s.rejected_because: an order of magnitude above the measured transient: forcerange/I ~ 94-98 rad/s^2 is the acceleration ceiling of a kp=14, I~0.062 wrist hinge, and tau_s = 0.2857 s is a window the command rate gives, not the servo.  A bound an order of magnitude above every achievable value gates nothing.

replay.video_to_ctrl_alignment: video t = (frame-1)/3 s; control t = k/20 s; commands linearly resampled, endpoints preserved
replay.fps_scope: execution (servo command / physics) frames at the scene's 20 Hz control rate; t = k/fps. Timeline: 16 video-driven frames (0.80 s) + 32 blend frames into the v5 gate3 seed + 30 hold frames. The source clip runs at an effective 3.0 fps (runs/p0/assets/frames/f_NNNN = source frame 10*(NN-1)+1) and runs/w6b/mano_params.npz stays on that video timeline (t=(N-1)/3); video frame N sits at t=(N-1)/3 on this axis.

gate1_final_touch.criterion: v5.1 (GPT round-3): >= 2 pads per hand with pad-centre rectangle distance <= R5 (mid-face band), simultaneously both hands; pad-centroid forward axis <= 35 deg; no burial; palm free
gate1_final_touch.pass_basis: v5.1 on the command-terminal configuration (>=2 pads in rect + forward axis); palm free by ruling

executed_state_evidence.note: post-contact-physics final state, identical metric: the solver keeps pad SURFACES on the face so pad centres ride ~pad-radius off the plane

servo_winding_position.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per finger joint: (1) excess beyond jnt_range <= |forcerange|/kp, (2) at most 3 consecutive control frames (150 ms at 20 Hz), (3) the transient is elastic wind-up: there is a contact torque on that DoF, the actuator is not on its force limit while it happens, and kp*(ctrl-qpos) accounts for the whole non-actuator load on the DoF to 5%. An excursion during saturation is never exempted, and neither is one on a freely drifting joint.

servo_winding_rate_hinge.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per wrist hinge: (1) realised rate <= |forcerange|/dof_damping, (2) at most 3 consecutive control intervals above that same cap, (3) every interval in which the servo outran the command-side trackable rate 1.5 rad/s has its excess over the commanded rate explained as this DoF's own wind-up release (release_j(t) = sqrt(kp_j * windup_j(t)^2 / (dof_M0_j + armature_j)), windup_j(t) = ctrl_j(t) - qpos_j(t)) with the actuator off its force limit. kv = 0 does not weaken the bound: dof_damping = 1.2 is what makes a finite bound exist at all. The bound is tight -- the free-space step asymptote of this servo plateaus at 4.90-4.97 rad/s (both directions, both step signs), within 2% of it; with dof_damping forced to 0 the plateau disappears entirely.

dv <= a_max * tau_s.rejected_because: an order of magnitude above the measured transient: forcerange/I ~ 94-98 rad/s^2 is the acceleration ceiling of a kp=14, I~0.062 wrist hinge, and tau_s = 0.2857 s is a window the command rate gives, not the servo. servo_winding_rate_slide.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per wrist hinge: (1) realised rate <= |forcerange|/dof_damping, (2) at most 3 consecutive control intervals above that same cap, (3) every interval in which the servo outran the command-side trackable rate 0.2 rad/s has its excess over the commanded rate explained as this DoF's own wind-up release (release_j(t) = sqrt(kp_j * windup_j(t)^2 / (dof_M0_j + armature_j)), windup_j(t) = ctrl_j(t) - qpos_j(t)) with the actuator off its force limit. kv = 0 does not weaken the bound: dof_damping = 1.2 is what makes a finite bound exist at all. The bound is tight -- the free-space step asymptote of this servo plateaus at 4.90-4.97 rad/s (both directions, both step signs), within 2% of it; with dof_damping forced to 0 the plateau disappears entirely.

dv <= a_max * tau_s.rejected_because: an order of magnitude above the measured transient: forcerange/I ~ 94-98 rad/s^2 is the acceleration ceiling of a kp=14, I~0.062 wrist hinge, and tau_s = 0.2857 s is a window the command rate gives, not the servo.  A bound an order of magnitude above every achievable value gates nothing.

findings.consequence: the executed terminal cannot reproduce the seed's deep curls; the >=2-pad terminal criterion needs either servo/spring re-budget (scene generation) or a hold-feasible seed family
